Structurally related ionizable fluoroquinolone antibacterials (levofloxacin, ofloxacin, antofloxacin) show systemic availability approaching or reaching 100% in humans, demonstrating that ionized small-molecule antibacterials can be well absorbed.
The polar nucleoside analog doxifluridine shows ~50-80% oral bioavailability in patients, illustrating that a polar small molecule can still achieve high systemic availability.

Additional heteroaromatic small molecules in the evidence set (asciminib, compound 109, LY2196044, the pyrazolopyrimidinone, pradigastat, zidovudine) have F values of 34-73%, all above the 20% threshold.

All visible L1 contexts are positive examples; there is no low-F comparator to calibrate transfer.
The physicochemical prior is based solely on properties and does not include transporter or prodrug-conversion data.
